newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Treasurer asks for SEC probe of bond deals.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Treasurer asks for SEC probe of bond deals.

text.p: California state Treasurer Matt Fong called on the Securities and Exchange Commission and the state Attorney General to investigate several municipal securities transactions in the state.
Fong called for the investigations in letters to SEC Chairman Arthur Levitt and Attorney General Dan Lungren. The letters were obtained by Reuters late on Wednesday.
Fong's office confirmed that the letters, dated Sept 10, were sent, but said the Treasurer would not comment on them until Thursday's meeting of the California Debt Advisory Commission.
"I am writing to request your investigation of certain recent municipal securities transactions in California that threaten the integrity of the municipal market," Fong said in his letter to Levitt.

Fong referred to a series of transactions conducted under the state's Marks-Roos Local Bond Pooling Act, which authorizes the formation of joint powers agencies to finance capital projects of local government agencies.
Fong's office declined to provide the list of transactions to Reuters, but sources said the list included nine deals underwritten by Pacific Genesis Group Inc.

The joint powers agencies in these transactions were formed by several local agencies, in return for a cash payment from the bond proceeds, to issue bonds. The bonds were used by developers to pay for capital improvements in other areas of the state. Indian tribes were represented to be the "local agencies" on whose behalf the bonds were issued, Fong said.
Fong said these offerings violated the "letter and spirit" of state law.
"In my view, these practices violate state laws, raise federal securities law concerns, and harm the interests of the issuer community in general," Fong said in the letter.
Fong said these bond sales appear to have been conducted in violation of state laws for essentially private purposes.

"If federal and state securities laws are not enforced against those persons responsible for these transactions, others may be encouraged to undertake even more creative, risky, and illegal transactions in the future," Fong said in the letter.
He sent similar letters to Lungren, as well as officials with the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board, an industry regulatory panel in Washington, and the California State Bar Association.

Fong said existing state and federal laws and regulations should be used to discourage these kinds of transactions and "encourage a new respect for the conservative legal approach that has traditionally been fundamental to municipal bond transactions."

"I believe that much of this authority lies in the hands of the SEC, the MSRB, the state Attorney General and the State Bar Association, and I respectfully offer the cooperation of my office in its exercise," Fong said.
Pacific Genesis was not immediately available to comment on Treasurer Fong's letter.
